metadata.title: ValGuide
metadata.description: Digital guides for exhibitions, museums, and public tours.

hero.title: The Studio-style workflow for museum guides.
hero.description: ValGuide lets cultural teams publish multilingual audio and text guides on the web, without app-store friction, rented devices, or agency-style rebuilds.
hero.proofEyebrow: Real product, not a concept deck
hero.proofTitle: One publishing workflow from tour setup to launch.
hero.proofBody: The product already covers content editing, translations, branding, QR distribution, and practical rollout work inside one Studio.
hero.proofAlt: ValGuide Studio tour editor with language-specific content, media, and theme controls

screenshots.title: The system already looks like a working product because it is one.
screenshots.description: Compared with agency microsites, shared visitor platforms, or heavyweight native apps, ValGuide stays focused on one strong publishing workflow.

tours.label: Tours overview
tours.title: See every guide in one operational view.
tours.body: Teams can launch, review, and manage multiple tours without turning daily publishing into project management.
tours.alt: ValGuide Studio tours list showing multiple museum guide cards

editor.label: Editorial workflow
editor.title: Edit language-specific content where the work happens.
editor.body: Tour structure, copy, media, and translations stay in one place so updates do not bounce between tools.
editor.alt: ValGuide Studio editor for language-specific tour content

brand.label: Brand control
brand.title: Apply your institution's visual identity without a custom rebuild.
brand.body: Teams can tune colors, surfaces, and presentation directly in the Studio instead of opening a new design project.
brand.alt: ValGuide Studio brand customizer with theme presets and color controls

problem.title: Most alternatives create work around the guide instead of improving the guide itself.
problem.description: The competitor landscape is crowded, but the operational pain repeats: too much hardware, too much project overhead, and too little editorial control.

apps.title: Native apps add release overhead
apps.body: App-store review, device testing, and version maintenance slow down launches that should stay simple.

hardware.title: Hardware fleets create logistics
hardware.body: Charging, cleaning, storage, and replacement work lands on museum teams instead of staying with the content.

content.title: Updates depend on outside help
content.body: Small editorial changes often turn into tickets, partner handoffs, or new project scope.

accessibility.title: Accessibility gets bolted on late
accessibility.body: Too many solutions treat accessibility as an add-on instead of part of the core visitor flow.

budget.title: Budgets disappear into setup work
budget.body: Money goes into infrastructure and project management instead of content quality and reach.

temporary.title: Temporary shows still need a good solution
temporary.body: Short exhibitions often cannot justify a heavy rollout, even when visitors clearly need guidance.

solution.title: ValGuide keeps the value in publishing speed, control, and visitor access.
solution.description: Instead of spreading work across apps, agencies, and devices, teams run one workflow for creation, localization, brand control, and launch.

web.title: Browser-first delivery
web.body: Visitors open the guide instantly on their own phones. No download, no install, no app-store dependency.

brand.title: Institution-ready branding
brand.body: Apply your visual identity inside the product instead of paying for a custom visual layer every time.

ai.title: AI supports editing work
ai.body: Use AI where it saves curator time, while keeping review and final decisions human.

languages.title: Translations stay in the workflow
languages.body: Language variants live next to the core content, so multilingual publishing stays operationally sane.

accessibility.title: Accessibility stays visible
accessibility.body: Readable layouts, audio support, and assistive features stay part of the default experience.

analytics.title: Practical rollout control
analytics.body: Publishing, QR distribution, and iteration stay inside one system that teams can actually operate.

step1.title: Set up the guide once
step1.body: Build stops, copy, media, and translations in one place.

step2.title: Publish one stable visitor entry point
step2.body: Use a web link or QR code across signage, print, and campaigns.

step3.title: Improve without rebuilding
step3.body: Update the live guide as exhibitions change, without starting another app or agency project.

why.title: A better fit than rented hardware, shared museum platforms, or another custom build.
why.description: The product is deliberately narrow: a white-label, browser-first guide workflow for institutions that want control without operational drag.

audio.title: Compared with hardware-based guides
audio.point1: No device fleet to manage, charge, clean, or replace.
audio.point2: Visitors use the phones they already carry.
audio.point3: Temporary exhibitions stay viable without rental logistics.

apps.title: Compared with native visitor apps
apps.point1: Faster to launch because the browser is already installed.
apps.point2: No app-store friction for visitors on-site.
apps.point3: Smaller scope means fewer moving parts to support.

agencies.title: Compared with agency-led builds
agencies.point1: The institution keeps ownership after launch.
agencies.point2: Updates do not become a new scoped project each time.
agencies.point3: The workflow stays with the team that knows the content.

useCases.title: Designed for formats that need speed without compromise.
useCases.description: The strongest fit is any guide format where browser access, multilingual publishing, and lean operations matter more than platform sprawl.

permanent.title: Permanent collections
permanent.body: Keep one stable guide layer live and improve it over time without re-platforming.

temporary.title: Temporary exhibitions
temporary.body: Launch quickly for a limited run without justifying a custom app or device fleet.

multilingual.title: Multilingual audiences
multilingual.body: Offer multiple languages without splitting the workflow across documents and vendors.

accessibility.title: Accessibility-led interpretation
accessibility.body: Support visitors with readable layouts, audio, and lower-friction access from the start.

education.title: Educational and guided formats
education.body: Reuse the same publishing foundation for tours, school groups, and interpretive storytelling.

tourism.title: Public walking tours
tourism.body: Publish outdoor or city guides with the same web-first model used inside institutions.

pricing.title: Pricing shaped around rollout reality.
pricing.description: We scope pricing around exhibition scale, publishing complexity, and the support your team actually needs.
pricing.philosophy: The goal is not the biggest package. The goal is a guide workflow your team can launch and keep running.

starter.label: Starter
starter.description: For smaller institutions or first launches validating the workflow.

professional.label: Professional
professional.description: For institutions running multiple guides and recurring updates.

enterprise.label: Enterprise
enterprise.description: For larger organizations with tighter coordination and rollout planning needs.

pricing.offsetBody: We scope against your exhibition format, languages, and operational constraints instead of forcing you through a fake pricing calculator.

pilot.title: Start with a pilot that proves the visitor flow before scaling.
pilot.description: A pilot is the fastest way to validate fit, align stakeholders, and check the setup in a real exhibition context.

step1.title: Pick one exhibition or route
step1.body: Choose a contained case with real visitor value and manageable scope.

step2.title: Publish the first visitor experience
step2.body: Launch the guide with the core structure, branding, and access flow in place.

step3.title: Review usage and editorial feedback
step3.body: Check what visitors use and where the team needs adjustments.

step4.title: Expand with confidence
step4.body: Use the pilot learnings to scale to additional tours, languages, or venues.

trust.title: ValGuide is designed around publishing work, not feature theater.
trust.body: The product focus is simple: help cultural teams get digital visitor guidance live with less friction, stronger ownership, and fewer moving parts.
trust.trustPoint2: No hardware fleet for staff to manage.
trust.trustPoint3: One place to update content and translations.
trust.trustPoint4: A setup that can survive real museum operations.

footer.description: Digital visitor guides for museums, exhibitions, and public tours.
